When your rucking progress stalls

Training · practical guide

Use a familiar route to work out what is holding you back.

Read article: When your rucking progress stalls
01

Rucking form that holds up

Fit your pack, keep the load secure and pay attention to how you move as distance increases.

  • Adjust the pack before you start.
  • Notice when your posture changes late in a ruck.
  • Build distance and load separately when possible.
02

Fuel longer rucks

Long events call for a practical food and water plan, not guesswork on the day.

  • Try food and drinks during training.
  • Know where you can refill water.
  • Bring a spare option if you have trouble eating while moving.
03

Make hard sessions worthwhile

A demanding shared ruck is a chance to practise teamwork and learn how you respond when the route gets uncomfortable.

  • Set a real challenge, not just a vague promise to push harder.
  • Keep group communication simple.
  • Afterward, note one thing to repeat and one thing to change.
04

Rucking with a purpose

A ruck can support endurance, fitness, team connection, event preparation or community work. Choose which purpose you are training for.

  • Pick an outcome you can observe.
  • Use the same route or test to compare progress.
  • Build shared challenges that leave room for different abilities.
